skill.name: iterate-pr
skill.description: Automates pull request iteration by checking CI, collecting review feedback, applying targeted fixes, committing changes, and waiting for checks to pass.
skill.summary: Iterate on GitHub pull requests until CI and review feedback are resolved.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate pull request automation workflow, but it relies on GitHub CLI, git, and jq commands. Most backtick detections are Markdown false positives; the meaningful risks are the unquoted branch command substitution and the broad git add, commit, and push flow. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Broad staging and pushing can publish unintended files.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit user review before commit and push, and show the staged diff before publishing changes.

remediation.issue: git add -A stages every workspace change.
remediation.suggestion: Stage only files changed to fix the validated CI or review issue, and avoid untracked or generated files by default.

remediation.issue: The branch lookup uses unquoted shell command substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Store the branch name in a variable and quote it when passing it to GitHub CLI commands.

remediation.issue: Authenticated GitHub commands run in the user repository context.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the skill should run only in trusted repositories with least-privilege GitHub credentials.

static_findings.snippet: The `bucket` field categorizes state into: `pass`, `fail`, `pending`, `skipping`, or `cancel`.
**Important:** If any of these checks are still `pending`, wait before proceeding:
- All CI checks are green (`bucket: pass`)
- Use `gh pr checks --required` to focus only on required checks
- Use `gh run view <run-id> --verbose` to see all job steps, not just failures
4. **Skip invalid feedback** - If the concern is not legitimate, move on

content.user_title: Iterate Pull Requests Until CI Passes
content.value_statement: Failed checks and scattered review comments slow pull request work. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a repeatable fix, push, and verify loop.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the current GitHub pull request for the active branch.
Checks CI status and waits for important pending bot checks.
Collects review comments, inline comments, and bot feedback from GitHub.
Reads failed GitHub Actions logs before proposing fixes.
Applies targeted code changes, commits them, pushes them, and watches CI status.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI and a local branch with an open pull request.
Assumes GitHub pull requests and GitHub Actions style checks.
Can stage, commit, and push local changes when the workflow reaches that step.
Stops for repeated failures, unclear review feedback, missing PRs, or branch sync issues.

use_cases.title: Repair a Failing Pull Request
use_cases.description: Use the skill to inspect failing checks, read logs, make targeted fixes, and verify the updated PR.

use_cases.title: Resolve Review and Bot Feedback
use_cases.description: Use the skill to gather human comments and automated tool feedback before editing the branch.

use_cases.title: Prepare a PR for Merge
use_cases.description: Use the skill to focus on required checks and repeat the verification loop until the PR is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Current PR Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a branch that already has an open pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr on my current branch. Check the PR status, read any failed CI logs, make minimal fixes, and report what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Review Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Review-focused workflow after CI and bot checks finish.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr to collect review comments and bot feedback for this PR. Validate each issue before editing, then address only valid items.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Specific Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow when one workflow or job is failing repeatedly.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr to inspect the failing GitHub Actions logs for this PR. Find the root cause, make a focused fix, and rerun the check loop.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Merge Readiness Loop
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for repeated CI and review iterations before merge.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr until all required checks pass and no validated feedback remains. Stop after three repeated failures or if a product decision is needed.

output_examples.input: A pull request has failed tests and a Codecov comment.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the failed workflow, validates the coverage concern, applies a targeted fix, and watches the next check run.

output_examples.input: A reviewer requests a change that may already be fixed.
output_examples.output: The skill checks the current code, determines whether the feedback is still valid, and either fixes it or explains why no change was needed.

output_examples.input: A PR has pending Sentry and required GitHub checks.
output_examples.output: The skill waits for important pending checks before making more changes, then continues only when actionable feedback is available.

best_practices: Start from a clean branch so broad staging cannot include unrelated work.
Review the final diff before allowing any commit or push step.
Ask for user input when failures repeat or feedback requires a decision.
anti_patterns: Running the workflow with unrelated local changes in the workspace.
Guessing a fix from a check name without reading the failure logs.
Treating every bot or reviewer comment as valid without checking the code.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates a pull request loop for checking CI, reading feedback, making fixes, pushing changes, and waiting for results.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires an authenticated gh command and a local branch linked to a GitHub pull request.

faq.question: Can it work with non-GitHub CI systems?
faq.answer: It is designed around GitHub pull requests and GitHub Actions style checks. Other systems may need manual adaptation.

faq.question: Does it change repository files?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow can make code edits, stage files, create commits, and push the branch when fixes are ready.

faq.question: How does it handle unreliable feedback?
faq.answer: It tells the agent to validate each failure or comment before editing, and to skip feedback that is not legitimate.

faq.question: When should the workflow stop?
faq.answer: It should stop when checks pass, when no PR exists, when the branch needs sync work, or when repeated failures need help.
